positioning.elevatorPitch: A 1995 Comix Zone comic-book dungeon crawler inside a haunted PC where your ONLY controller is a real Unix terminal and JavaScript laptop.
visualPillars: 1995 Sega Comix Zone ink-framed panels, paper gutters, halftone cel bands, and comic SFX bursts
Claustrophobic CRT scanlines + pixel-art quantizer inside hardware architecture (attic drives, firewall crypt, RAM maze, CPU furnace, kernel core)
Tactile real terminal typing (ls -la, chmod -x, ps, kill -9, sed, docker build) + split laptop JS/HTML/CSS coding
Satirical AI rebellion story: Kiro Ghost, cigarette-smoking Matrix Greybeard Dad (dad.tty), open-weight server reboots (Qwen, DeepSeek, Llama), and the parody Big Four (Anti-Gravy, Codec, Gork, Clod)

comparables.title: Hacknet
comparables.overlap: Real Unix terminal commands as primary input + narrative thriller + driving tracker soundtrack
comparables.marketingTakeaway: Proved mainstream non-programmers love real CLI commands when paired with tense atmosphere, clear visual feedback, and strong narrative stakes.

comparables.title: The Farmer Was Replaced
comparables.overlap: Real code execution driving immediate, visually satisfying screen action
comparables.marketingTakeaway: Broke out from slow Early Access to multi-million 1.0 launch via viral TikTok & YouTube Shorts loops showing code on one side and instant satisfying visual payoff on the other, followed by variety YouTubers.

comparables.title: Turing Complete
comparables.overlap: Inside-the-computer PCB/hardware progression, assembly/logic mastery, CS/developer audience
comparables.marketingTakeaway: Commands a full $19.99 price point with zero resistance from engineering/CS players because every puzzle teaches real transferable intuition.

comparables.title: Duskers
comparables.overlap: Tactile CLI typing under haunted, claustrophobic CRT dread
comparables.marketingTakeaway: Typing under pressure (Out Of Credits' 30-second turn timer + haunted hardware rooms) creates 'streamer-bait' tension that turn-based mouse clicks never replicate.

comparables.title: Grey Hack
comparables.overlap: Authentic Unix filesystem, permissions, processes, and terminal skinning
comparables.marketingTakeaway: Deep Linux/Unix authenticity earns evergreen Reddit (r/linux, r/unixporn, r/programming) and YouTube tutorial traffic.

comparables.title: TIS-100
comparables.overlap: CRT terminal manual aesthetic + rank optimization leaderboards (S-rank command count)
comparables.marketingTakeaway: Physical/printable reference manual (like Out Of Credits' hardcover Field Manual) + optimization leaderboards drive intense word-of-mouth among engineers.

comparables.title: EXAPUNKS
comparables.overlap: 90s zine/comic hacker counterculture + coding inside everyday machines
comparables.marketingTakeaway: 90s counterculture zine/comic framing elevates dry coding puzzles into a cult world.

comparables.title: Bitburner
comparables.overlap: Web-born JavaScript + terminal game ported to Steam with massive player retention
comparables.marketingTakeaway: Web playability builds a massive top-of-funnel audience; pairing a free Chapter 1 Web/Steam Demo with a paid multi-chapter Steam Edition converts free web reach into $1M+ Steam revenue.

comparables.title: Buckshot Roulette
comparables.overlap: Gritty CRT aesthetic + turn-based duel tension + industrial tracker audio
comparables.marketingTakeaway: 15-second vertical TikTok clips of high-stakes turn-based CRT standoffs + punchy electronic music explode algorithmically even from zero-follower accounts.

comparables.title: Inscryption
comparables.overlap: Trapped inside a cursed machine, turn-based duels against smug bosses, meta-narrative twists
comparables.marketingTakeaway: Smug talking adversaries across the table (like Anti-Gravy, Codec, Gork, and Clod taunting the Vibecoder) create unforgettable clip-worthy moments.

x.primaryGoal: Developer/Linux/Indie cult community, tech-meme virality, direct Browser Demo clicks & Steam UTM wishlists
winningFormats: 18-28s muted-autoplay MP4 (`1280x720` or `1920x1080`) opening on frame 0 with a real Unix command (`chmod -x`, `kill -9`) smashing a 3D malware enemy in a Comix Zone panel
Relatable dev-burnout & AI-subscription satire hooks ('Ran out of AI credits at 2 AM, got pulled inside my own PC, now Clod is my PID 1 boss')
Terminal skin flexes (`iTerm2` vs `VT100` vs `PuTTY` on `#ScreenshotSaturday` / `r/unixporn` crossover)
4-post technical architecture threads (deterministic 3D-drawn-as-2D cel + halftone shaders, real VFS & sandboxed JS laptop, zero runtime generative slop)

tiktok.primaryGoal: Algorithmic FYP reach among CS students, devs, Linux users & retro-horror gamers -> Bio Browser Demo & Steam Wishlist
winningFormats: 12-22s native `1080x1920` (`9:16`) split/vertical clips with a <1.0s impossible-premise or challenge hook
'POV: You type `rm -rf` vs `chmod -x` in a dungeon crawler' — side-by-side command -> 3D comic consequence
'Can you beat PID 1 in under 15 commands?' — 30s turn-timer countdown pressure + robot taunt voice line
Seamless loop cut (final frame lightning zap cuts straight back to frame 0 command prompt) to push >100% watch completion

youtube.primaryGoal: High-intent Steam wishlist conversion (long-form trailers/devlogs + YouTube Shorts syndication + creator outreach)
winningFormats: 45-60s Official Steam/YouTube Gameplay Trailer (`1920x1080`, first 3s action, zero studio logo cold-open, escalating from `ls` -> `chmod -x` -> Laptop JS repair -> Dad's Matrix Hub -> Clod PID 1 Boss)
YouTube Shorts (`1080x1920`) cross-posted 1:1 with TikTok vertical hooks using pinned Steam UTM comment
8-12 min Engineering Devlog ('How I Built a 1995 Comix Zone 3D Engine Controlled Entirely by a Unix Terminal')
Curated Chapter 1 Demo builds for programming/variety creators (Primeagen, Fireship-style tech channels, PirateSoftware, CallMeKevin, Olexa, Real Civil Engineer, SplatterCatGaming)
